correctness.rationale: The orthogonal monomial norms yield the exact scalar kernel. On |t|=1 the identity F_m=-4 sin²(theta/2) exp(i(m+1)theta) proves all and only boundary crossing parameters. The logarithmic derivative has real part m+1 and implies strictly inward crossing, so the root count follows from the argument principle. The sole critical multiple-root strength q*=(m+2)^(m+2)/(4m^m) exceeds m+1, hence every physically accessible interior root is simple. Every scalar |t|<1 is attainable by a disk pair. Finite numerical tests m=1..14 agree but are not used to prove the result.

value.rationale: Discrete point-derivative penalties are standard Sobolev-type regularizations, while zero-freeness of Bergman reproducing kernels is a natural Lu Qi-Keng invariant. For every derivative order the result gives a complete exact spectrum of first and subsequent zero entries, conjugate-pair multiplicities, inward crossing monotonicity and an explicit physically reachable penalty test. The parity distinction and partial higher-degree staircase are structural rather than an arbitrary isolated coefficient calculation; general extensions remain open.
